title: Client Standing Across All Professional Services Projects Engagements
content:
For Professional Services Projects, work on any engagement depends on the client's standing across all of its engagements.

## Standing condition

A project may kick off or resume only while no engagement of the client has an invoice past due by more than that engagement's work stoppage threshold (the number of days an engagement invoice may be past due before work is put on hold for non-payment, set by that engagement's class). An engagement put on hold for non-payment resumes only once that condition holds again.

## How the past-due figure is read

- The figure is taken at a point in time across every engagement of the client: the largest number of days any unpaid project invoice of the client is past its due date.
- An invoice's due date is its posted date plus the net payment terms of the class of the engagement it belongs to.
- Each invoice is measured against the work stoppage threshold of its own engagement, not the threshold of the engagement that is to kick off or resume.
- The evidence is the system record of the client's project billing: the invoices, their kinds, amounts and posted dates. A statement by the caller about what has been paid does not replace those records, and the check is made before kickoff or resumption.

## Condition table

| Any invoice of the client past due by more than its own engagement's threshold? | Kickoff or resumption of any engagement |
|---|---|
| No | may proceed under this condition |
| Yes | may not proceed |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)

- An unpaid invoice on a Standard Project, whose threshold is hypothetically taken as 30 days, is past due by exactly 30 days: it is not past due by more than 30 days, so the condition still holds.
- The same invoice one day later is past due by 31 days: no engagement of that client may kick off or resume until the condition holds again.
- An engagement on hold for non-payment stays on hold while any invoice of the client remains past due by more than its own engagement's threshold.
